Container.Name: bookbandit
Container.Overview: Bookbandit is a self-hosted family book library and reader. It reads your ebooks and comics from a plain folder, gives every family member their own shelves, progress and bookmarks that sync between devices, and keeps kids to age-appropriate books. Calibre's ebook-convert and kepubify are built in for format conversion.[br][br]Put it behind a reverse proxy with Tinyauth (or another forward-auth provider) and set Trusted proxies to that proxy's IP or Docker network.
Container.Requires: Nothing extra: the first person to open the web UI creates the admin account with a username and password. Optional: a reverse proxy with Tinyauth for Google sign-in.

Config.Name: WebUI port
Config.Description: Port for the web app and API.

Config.Name: Config
Config.Description: Database, covers and caches. Keep this on the cache pool.

Config.Name: Books
Config.Description: Your book library (plain files). Bookbandit never changes file ownership here.

Config.Name: Audiobooks
Config.Description: Optional: audiobook folders, one per book (the folder Audiobookshelf uses works as is).

Config.Name: Trusted proxies
Config.Description: Comma-separated IPs or CIDRs of your reverse proxy (for example 172.18.0.0/16). Sign-in headers from anywhere else are ignored. Empty means nobody can sign in through the proxy.

Config.Name: Auth email header
Config.Description: Header your proxy sets with the signed-in email. Tinyauth uses remote-email.

Config.Name: Google sign-in URL
Config.Description: Optional. Your Tinyauth login page; shows a Sign in with Google button. Username and password sign-in works without it.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User id that owns files Bookbandit writes (99 = nobody on Unraid).

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group id that owns files Bookbandit writes (100 = users on Unraid).

Config.Name: UMASK
Config.Description: File permission mask for new files. Use 002 to let the users group write.

Config.Name: Time zone
Config.Description: Your time zone (for example America/Chicago), so the nightly backup runs at night where you are. Empty means UTC.

Config.Name: Backup time
Config.Description: When the nightly database backup runs (HH:MM), or off. Backups go to /config/backups.

Config.Name: Backups to keep
Config.Description: How many nightly backups to keep. 0 keeps them all.

Config.Name: Log level
Config.Description: fatal, error, warn, info, debug or trace.
